MK: So, even if they are afebrile on presentation you can trust the rectal temperature at home.
There is no evidence to support the use of forehead strip thermometers.
In spite of evidence in support of temporal thermometers, rectal temperatures are preferred in this age group and the majority of published data use rectal temperatures.
So, you can’t just “add a degree” to get the core temperature. If a child has a fever by axillary measurement (without adding a degree) it is an accurate representation of fever.
Caregivers tend to overestimate fever in infants
